description: The 56-member bi-partisan Problem Solvers Caucus (PSC) seeks an innovative, strategic, and experienced communications director based in Washington, D.C. The staff member in this position proactively promotes and helps build the caucus's national image and manage its press, social media, and communications operations. The communications director works closely with the executive director, PSC co-chairs and their staff to carry out assigned duties. This position is responsible for helping plan, draft, and coordinate communications activities to advance caucus priorities, including pitching stories, developing social media content, writing press releases, and maintaining positive working relationships with members of national, state, and local media. The communications director produces caucus-oriented talking points, member media toolkits, and works collaboratively with member offices. This is not an entry-level position. Salary range for this position is $50,000 to $56,000 plus benefits. Applications will be taken through March 10, 2021.

Write press releases
Maintain positive working relationships with members of national, state, and local media
Produce caucus-oriented talking points and member media toolkits
Work collaboratively with member offices
qualifications: At least two years of previous communications experience, including Capitol Hill experience
Relationships with the congressional press corps
Disposition aligned with the caucus mission of breaking the gridlock in Congress by promoting bi-partisan, bi-cameral collaboration and policies
Strong writing, communication, and organizational skills
Digital and social media savviness
Creativity

Familiarity with graphic design, website and social media design
Ability to construct and convey messages to a national audience through print, television, and digital media
how_to_apply: Submit a cover letter, resume, short writing sample, and at least two professional references to Jaclyn.ODay@mail.house.gov, with the subject line as "Problem Solvers Caucus Communications Director."
equal_opportunity: The Problem Solvers Caucus is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including marital or parental status), sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age, national origin, or service in the military.
